haiku-low.q1: Probes seeing 2 of 3 locations with 3 consecutive /healthz failures pages on-call only. Nothing happens automatically. A person runs the failover command.
haiku-low.q2: It stops with nothing changed, unless an explicit accept-data-loss override is given. The prompt also shows how long ago B last received WAL.
haiku-low.q3: Before promotion: A fenced (record FENCING, then FENCED, after a 45 s wait). Before B's workers start: B's database promoted and writable, and running jobs requeued. Before DNS: B's app scaled to 12 and passing its health check.
haiku-low.q4: It is lost. Users signed in at failover time must sign in again, because B's Redis is empty and sessions are not replicated.
haiku-low.q5: It is never reused as primary. It stays stopped or read-only, is rebuilt as a replica of B, and its divergent tail is exported first.
haiku-low.q6: A fences itself: its watchdog cannot renew the lease at epoch n+1, so it sets Postgres read-only then stops it. The command waits 45 s regardless.
haiku-low.q7: A small active-region record in a strongly consistent store outside both regions. The failover command writes it by compare-and-set and reads it on rerun. A's watchdog renews its lease.
haiku-low.q8: Before B's workers start, the command sets every running row to pending and adds 1 to attempts. Jobs must be safe to run twice, so external side effects need idempotency keys.
haiku-low.q9: Rerun the same command; it reads the record, checks B's state, and resumes at the first unfinished step. Return to A is possible only before promotion, via the documented abort. After PROMOTED there is no way back.
haiku-low.q10: Cached DNS keeps pointing at dead A until the 60 s TTL expires. The document does not describe the client experience further: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Up to the unreplicated tail, which can exceed 30 s. The target is 30 s, gated on B's replay lag at 30 s or less, but the gate cannot see later writes.

sonnet.q1: A person starts failover by running the single failover command after on-call is paged. Detection (2 of 3 probe locations see 3 consecutive /healthz failures) only pages on-call; it never fails over automatically.
sonnet.q2: The lag gate reads B's last recorded replay lag. If over 30 s, the command stops with nothing changed, and continues only with an explicit accept-data-loss override (it also prints how long ago B last received WAL next to the prompt).
sonnet.q3: Before B's database is promoted: A must be fenced (record at FENCING, wait of lease plus margin = 45 s, best-effort cloud API stop, then state FENCED). Before B's workers start: B's database is writable (promoted) and the running-to-pending requeue is done. Before DNS moves: B's app is scaled up (2 to 12) and passing its health check.
sonnet.q4: Sessions are lost. B's Redis is empty (not replicated), so signed-in users must sign in again. This is accepted.
sonnet.q5: It is never reused as primary. Its Postgres stays stopped or read-only; A is rebuilt as a replica of B. Its divergent tail is exported and kept for manual reconciliation before old data is discarded. Moving back is a separate planned switchover.
sonnet.q6: Fencing by the lease and watchdog. The watchdog on A's database host renews a 30 s lease only against its own epoch. Once the record is at n+1 renewals fail, and when the lease runs out the watchdog sets Postgres read-only and then stops it, timed on a monotonic clock. The command waits 45 s (lease plus 15 s margin) before promoting B, whether or not any API call to A worked.
sonnet.q7: The active-region record {active, epoch, state, lease_expiry}, held in a strongly consistent store (3-node consensus store or managed equivalent) in a separate region or provider. The failover command writes it via compare-and-set (FENCING, FENCED, PROMOTED, ACTIVE) and reads it on reruns; A's watchdog reads/renews the lease against it. Nothing else is stated about other readers.
sonnet.q8: Rows marked running are replicated to B but their workers are gone. After promotion and before B's workers start, one idempotent statement sets every running row to pending and adds 1 to attempts. Jobs must be safe to run twice (idempotency keys for external side effects). Jobs in the unreplicated tail are lost or reverted.
sonnet.q9: Rerun the same command. It keeps no local state, reads the record and checks whether B's database is still in recovery, and resumes at the first unfinished step. Going back to A is possible only before promotion (state FENCING or FENCED), by running the documented abort, which writes epoch n+2 with A active; A may need a restart if its watchdog already stopped Postgres. After PROMOTED there is no way back.
sonnet.q10: NOT STATED. (The document says only that DNS has a 60 s TTL and moves to B after B's app is healthy; it does not describe what a client with a stale cache experiences.)
sonnet.q11: RPO target is 30 s, supported by the lag gate (replication is asynchronous). The gate only checks B's last recorded replay lag and cannot see writes A accepted after B last received WAL, so real loss can exceed the number and the 30 s RPO is not guaranteed. Anything in the unreplicated tail is lost. An accept-data-loss override can proceed despite larger lag.
